members.name: Jem Coombe
members.role: tenant of the Lakemead; pays Nell Sedge rent in grain; Elmwick folk have pulled down his fence twice

members.name: Tibbott Coombe
members.role: Jem's widowed father; too bent for heavy work but keeps the meadow's bees and the old tally of the rent
ties: grandfather of Cedda Coombe and Osric Coombe
remembers the meadow grazed by Elmwick and Reedmoor both before it was let
grudges Hob Garrow for the talk in Elmwick
keeps the bees and the rent tally

members.name: Rill Fenlake
members.role: fishes the southern lake from a flat punt and smokes the catch; lives in the old boathouse at the meadow's edge
ties: sells smoked fish to Thistle Mossfoot's packs
trades with Morwen Coombe for cheese and milk
grudges the Elmwick men who trampled her nets when they pulled the fence
friendly with Eadric Sedge of Reedmoor
owes Nell Sedge a share of the lake catch for the boathouse's standing

members.name: Gristle Fenlake
members.role: Rill's son; mends the punt and knows the shallow pools of the lake
ties: helps his mother smoke the catch
afraid of the deep water at the lake's middle

situations.summary: Elmwick says the Lakemead was always common grazing; Reedmoor's headwoman Nell Sedge let it to the Coombes for grain. Elmwick men have pulled down Jem's fence twice, and the Coombes keep mending it.

sides.Jem Coombe: He holds the meadow on a Reedmoor lease and pays rent in grain; he thinks Elmwick has no paper and no right, and he is tired of rebuilding fence posts.
sides.Morwen Coombe: She keeps the dairy going and trades cheese with Reedmoor folk, but she is friendly with Rowan Wray of Elmwick and hates that the quarrel sits between their families.
sides.Tibbott Coombe: He remembers when both villages grazed the meadow and thinks Nell Sedge was high-handed to let it; still, his son holds the lease and he will not see the Coombes turned off.

situations.summary: The Coombes owe Nell Sedge this year's rent in grain, and the harvest on the meadow strips has been thin; they have been paying part in cheese and labour and the rest is still owed.

sides.Jem Coombe: He is short of grain and does not want to ask Reedmoor for time again; he has thought of selling a goat but has not done it.
sides.Morwen Coombe: She has been carrying cheese to Hilda Sedge to make up the difference and worries Nell will take the meadow back if the grain does not come.
sides.Rill Fenlake: She owes Nell a share of the lake catch for her boathouse and knows the Coombes are behind; she has offered them smoked fish against their cheese, but she cannot cover their rent.

situations.summary: When Elmwick men pulled the fence down the second time, Rill Fenlake's nets were trampled where she had laid them to dry; she blames the Elmwick men and has said she will not sell fish to anyone from Elmwick.

sides.Rill Fenlake: She lost a good net and a morning's catch and thinks Elmwick folk came looking for a fight, not just a fence; she is angry and will not be talked round quickly.
sides.Jem Coombe: He mended the fence with Rill's help and feels he owes her; he would rather keep the quarrel with Elmwick than lose his neighbour's trade.
sides.Morwen Coombe: She thinks Rill is right to be angry but fears the fish trade with Elmwick was one of the few things keeping the meadow's households fed.

situations.summary: Thistle Mossfoot of Fernhollow comes through the Lakemead on the east road and has been friendly with the Coombes; Cedda Coombe follows him about asking for stories of the hollow, and Jem has half-promised to let her walk a stretch of the road with him when the packs are light.

sides.Jem Coombe: He likes Thistle and trusts him on the road, but the east road is no place for an eleven-year-old and he has not said yes outright.
sides.Morwen Coombe: She is fond of Thistle's visits and his fish, but she does not want her daughter walking roads with a pedlar's packs and has said so to Jem.
sides.Cedda Coombe: She wants to see Fernhollow and the giants' shelf beyond it, and she has already told Thea Wray she is going.
